--- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    zones_per_rank = total_zones / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(zones_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_zones / zones_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"zones_per_rank\": int(zones_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_zones_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of zones is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ZONES\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of zones per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ZONES\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ZONES\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n\n# --- Example Usage ---\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    \n    # Define the hardware once\n    hardware = {\n        \"cores_per_node\": 64,\n        \"memory_gb_per_node\": 256,\n        \"threading_hint\": 1\n    }\n    \n    # Scenario 1: Poor strong scaling (too few zones per rank)\n    print(\"--- Scenario 1: Poor Scaling ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=1000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=2e7,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected strategy_hint: \"INCREASE_ZONES\"\n\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*50 + \"\\n\")\n\n    # Scenario 2: Memory pressure (too many zones)\n    print(\"--- Scenario 2: High Memory Pressure ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=500000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=1e8,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected strategy_hint: \"DECREASE_ZONES\"\n\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*50 + \"\\n\")\n    \n    # Scenario 3: Good performance, close to optimal\n    print(\"--- Scenario 3: Optimal Performance -> STOP ---\")\n    result = evaluate_kripke_run(\n        total_zones=40000000,\n        total_ranks=64,\n        nodes_used=1,\n        current_fom=1.5e8,\n        threshold=0.95,\n        **hardware\n    )\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n    # Expected decision: \"STOP\"\n"
}

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# Per instructions, apt-get purge is not used.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# This makes the 'kripke' command directly available to the user and other applications.
# This uses the shell 'cp' command, not the Dockerfile 'COPY' instruction, to adhere to constraints.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# Per instructions, apt-get purge is not used.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# FIX: The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# This makes the 'kripke' command directly available to the user and other applications.
# This uses the shell 'cp' command, not the Dockerfile 'COPY' instruction, to adhere to constraints.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# FIX: The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# FIX: Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# This makes the 'kripke' command directly available to the user and other applications.
# This uses the shell 'cp' command, not the Dockerfile 'COPY' instruction, to adhere to constraints.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: Correct the path to the executable. With CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, CMake places
# the output in a 'Release' subdirectory within the build directory.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/Release/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: Correct the path to the executable. The default Unix Makefiles generator in Linux
# places the binary in 'build/bin', not 'build/Release/bin'.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: Corrected the path to the executable. With the Unix Makefiles generator,
# the binary is placed directly in the build directory, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.

ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: The executable is located directly in the build directory, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: The executable is located directly in the build directory, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: The executable is located in the 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications.
# The default 'cmake' package is removed and 'wget' is added to download a newer version.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies.
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is too old.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with both amd64 and arm64.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand, shared memory).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a requirement for this build.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, which is a standard practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# FIX: The executable is located directly in the build folder, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This will display Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build

# so we install 'wget' to download a newer version manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is insufficient.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with common architectures.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a common requirement in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# The default 'cmake' package from apt is too old for Kripke's dependencies,
# so we install 'wget' to download a newer version manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is insufficient.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with common architectures.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a common requirement in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source code is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This displays Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source code is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This displays Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# The default 'cmake' package from apt is too old for Kripke's dependencies,
# so we install 'wget' to download a newer version manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is insufficient.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with common architectures.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a common requirement in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source code is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This displays Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# The default 'cmake' package from apt is too old for Kripke's dependencies,
# so we install 'wget' to download a newer version manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is insufficient.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with common architectures.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a common requirement in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source code is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This displays Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04
# Provides a stable, well-supported base for the build.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates.
# We use --no-install-recommends to keep the image size smaller.
# The default 'cmake' package from apt is too old for Kripke's dependencies,
# so we install 'wget' to download a newer version manually.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a newer version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in the Ubuntu 22.04 apt repository (3.22.1) is insufficient.
# This downloads and installs a recent binary release compatible with common architectures.
ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.28.3
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    CMAKE_ARCH=""; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
        amd64) CMAKE_ARCH="x86_64"; ;; \
        arm64) CMAKE_ARCH="aarch64"; ;; \
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture: ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1; ;; \
    esac; \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${CMAKE_ARCH}.tar.gz -O cmake.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf cmake.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local && \
    rm cmake.tar.gz

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure MPI communicates over the container's virtual ethernet interface (eth0)
# and disables transports that are problematic or unavailable in containers (e.g., InfiniBand).
# We also explicitly allow running as root, which is a common requirement in containers.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary build location.
# This entire operation is done within the image, avoiding COPY/ADD instructions.
# The --recursive flag is essential to clone the necessary git submodules (e.g., BLT).
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/kripke

# Build Kripke from source using CMake.
# - ENABLE_MPI=ON is specified to meet the requirement for MPI support.
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release creates an optimized executable.
# The build is performed in a separate 'build' subdirectory, a standard CMake practice.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard location in the system's PATH.
# Kripke's build system places the final executable in a 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /opt/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the source code directory to reduce the final image size.
# The build tools and libraries remain, but the source code is no longer needed.
RUN rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a neutral working directory for the final image.
WORKDIR /

# Set the default command to run when the container starts.
# This displays Kripke's help message, confirming the build was successful and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]
